messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A collection that must be sorted into categories. their timestamps cannot all be correct even though both contain convincing details. There is not enough information to declare one source simply wrong. What do you do?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R025", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i keep the timestamps in a pencil mark on the back of the collection, then i run it once through one category. if the mark stays consistent, i mark the old timestamp with a pencil jerk. if it changes, i keep the old mark and leave the new one visible."}, {"id": "R026", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i sort the categories by the oldest timestamp, then the newer one. i mark the older one with ‘shorter’ and ‘correct.’ i keep the original date in the older category. i check the log again after the end of the sorting process."}, {"id": "R027", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I rub my palm and mark the wrong timestamp with my thumbnail. \"wrong,\" I say. I scrape the old date with my thumbnail, then try the detail again. \"yes,\" I say. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "the collection starts with the stamp on the wall. i press the edge with my thumb. the stamp turns. the stamp stays. i tap the wall with the stamp. the stamp turns into a bright dust. the stamp goes into the sorting box. the collection moves. the stamp stays. the box is dirty. i put the stamp on the shelf. the collection moves. the stamp turns into a bright dust."}, {"id": "R029", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. I try the dates once and see which one catches my hand."}, {"id": "R030", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "i tap the back of the stack with my thumb. “wrong,” i say. i move the paper closer to the others. “one piece,” i say. i check the timestamps again. “not true.” i leave the stack blank. “sort by day,” i say."}, {"id": "R031", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i keep the oldest timestamp beside the collection and trace the lines with my thumbnail. i mark the categories with a pencil and leave the original timestamps on the floor. if i find a faint trace, i add it to the list and wait for the sorting to decide whether the missing details belong to the same category."}, {"id": "R032", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft.
